indicators.name: Safety
indicators.desc: Students feel safe both in and around the school building.

indicators.name: School Safety
indicators.desc: Students encounter very little crime, violence, or bullying at school.

indicators.name: Student-Teacher Trust
indicators.desc: Students and teachers share a high level of mutual trust and respect.

indicators.name: Student Peer Relationships
indicators.desc: Students treat each other with respect, work well together, and help each other learn.

indicators.name: Parent Supportiveness
indicators.desc: Parents support their children emotionally and developmentally.

indicators.name: School Connectedness
indicators.desc: Students feel included in their school's community.

indicators.name: Emotional Health
indicators.desc: Students have the skills to nurture positive and respectful relationships with others.

indicators.name: Human & Social Resources in the Community
indicators.desc: Students come from communities where there are adults they can trust who provide a safe environment.

indicators.name: Rigorous Study Habits
indicators.desc: Students set aside time for schoolwork and give priority to studying.

indicators.name: Classroom Disruptions
indicators.desc: Teachers report on the degree to which other students disrupt their learning.

indicators.name: Collective Responsibility
indicators.desc: Teachers share a strong sense of responsibility for student development, school improvement, and professional growth.

indicators.name: Student Responsibility
indicators.desc: Students are active participants in their own learning and regularly attend class prepared to learn.

indicators.name: Parent Influence on Decision Making in Schools
indicators.desc: The school has created opportunities for parents to participate in developing academic programs and influencing school curricula.

indicators.name: Teacher-Parent Trust
indicators.desc: Teachers and parents are partners in improving student learning.

indicators.name: Parent Involvement in School
indicators.desc: Parents are active participants in their child's schooling.

indicators.name: Ambitious Instruction
indicators.desc: In schools with strong Ambitious Instruction, classes are challenging and engaging. The instruction is clear, well-structured, and encourages students to build and apply knowledge. When combined with a supportive environment, Ambitious Instruction has the most direct effect on student learning. It is: well-defined with clear expectations for student success, interactive and encourages students to build and apply knowledge, well-paced (not measured), and aligned across grades (not measured).

indicators.name: Collaborative Teachers
indicators.desc: In schools with strong Collaborative Teachers, all teachers collaborate to promote professional growth. In such schools, teachers are: active partners in school improvement, committed to the school, and focused on professional development.

indicators.name: Effective Leaders
indicators.desc: In schools with Effective Leaders, principals and teachers work together to implement a shared vision. In such schools, people, programs, and resources are focused on a vision for sustained improvement. Leaders: practice shared leadership, set high goals for quality instruction, maintain mutually trusting and respectful relationships, support professional advancement for faculty and staff, and manage resources for sustained program improvement (not measured).

indicators.name: Involved Families
indicators.desc: In schools with Involved Families, the entire staff builds strong external relationships. Such schools: see parents as partners in helping students learn, value parents' input and participation in advancing the school's mission, and support efforts to strengthen its students' community resources.

indicators.name: Supportive Environment
indicators.desc: In schools with a Supportive Environment, the school is safe, demanding, and supportive. In such schools: students feel safe in and around the school, they find teachers trust-worthy and responsive to their academic needs, all students value hard work, and teachers push all students toward high academic performance.

indicators.name: Academic Engagement
indicators.desc: Students are interested and engaged in learning.

indicators.name: Academic Personalism
indicators.desc: Teachers connect with students in the classroom and support them in achieving academic goals.

indicators.name: Academic Press
indicators.desc: Teachers expect students to do their best and to meet academic demands.

indicators.name: Classroom Rigor
indicators.desc: Teachers encourage all students to make connections and seek multiple perspectives through their coursework.

indicators.name: Collaborative Practices
indicators.desc: Teachers observe each others' practice and work together to review assessment data and develop instructional strategies.

indicators.name: Course Clarity
indicators.desc: Students are provided clear learning goals and instruction that supports achievement.

indicators.name: English Instruction
indicators.desc: Students interact with course material and one another to build and apply critical reading and writing skills.

indicators.name: Expectations for Postsecondary Education
indicators.desc: The school expects all students to attend college and promotes college-readiness.

indicators.name: Grit
indicators.desc: Students sustain interest and effort toward long-term goals.

indicators.name: Importance of High School for the Future
indicators.short: Importance of High School for the Future
indicators.desc: Students recognize that working hard during high school is important and that high school is preparing them for their life after graduation.

indicators.name: Innovation
indicators.desc: Teachers have a strong orientation toward improvement and a willingness to be a part of an active learning environment.

indicators.name: Inquiry-Based Science Instruction
indicators.desc: Students conduct scientific investigations, including generating and testing hypotheses, writing lab reports and using laboratory equipment.

indicators.name: Instructional Leadership
indicators.desc: The school leadership team sets high standards for teaching and student learning.

indicators.name: Math Instruction
indicators.desc: Students interact with course material and one another to build and apply knowledge in their math classes.

indicators.name: Peer Support for Academic Work
indicators.desc: Students demonstrate behaviors that lead to academic achievement.

indicators.name: Program Coherence
indicators.desc: School programs are coordinated and consistent with its goals for student learning.

indicators.name: Quality Professional Development
indicators.desc: Professional development is rigorous and focused on student learning.

indicators.name: Quality of Student Discussion
indicators.desc: Students participate in classroom discussions that build their critical thinking skills.

indicators.name: Reflective Dialogue
indicators.desc: Teachers frequently talk with each other about curriculum, instruction, and student learning.

indicators.name: School Commitment
indicators.desc: Teachers are deeply committed to the school.

indicators.name: School-Wide Future Orientation
indicators.desc: The school engages all students in planning for life after graduation.

indicators.name: Socialization of New Teachers
indicators.desc: New teachers are included in the professional community and are given helpful feedback on their instructional practices.

indicators.name: Teacher Influence
indicators.desc: Teachers have influence in a broad range of decisions regarding school policies and practices.

indicators.name: Teacher Safety
indicators.desc: Teachers report little or no disorder in the hallways, physical conflict among students, vandalism, robbery or theft, and threats of violence against teachers.

indicators.name: Teacher-Principal Trust
indicators.desc: Teachers and principals share a high level of mutual trust and respect.

indicators.name: Teacher-Teacher Trust
indicators.desc: Teachers are supportive and respectful of one another, personally and professionally.
